_meta.notes: Country-scoped curated nodes; link via relationships during ingest.

910.name: Early Inhabitants and Stone Age Settlements
910.label: Event
910.description: Early Stone Age occupation evidenced by tools at sites across Eswatini; San hunter-gatherers leave rock art; Ngwenya Mine is one of the world's oldest known mines.

910.name: Ngwenya Iron Ore Mine (Ancient)
910.label: Event
910.description: One of the world's oldest mines; San peoples mined haematite (red ochre) for cosmetic and ritual use around 43,000 years ago.

910.name: San Rock Art in Eswatini
910.label: Event
910.description: San/Bushmen rock paintings found across the country, particularly in the western highlands; depict hunting scenes and trance rituals.

920.name: Nguni Migration and Dlamini Dynasty Origins
920.label: Event
920.description: Nguni-speaking Bantu peoples migrate into the region; the Dlamini clan emerges as the ruling dynasty, establishing one of Africa's oldest continuous monarchies.

920.name: Bantu Migration and Settlement
920.label: Event
920.description: Nguni-speaking Bantu peoples arrive from East Africa via Mozambique; introduce iron-working, cattle herding, and agriculture; displace or absorb San populations.

920.name: Dlamini Dynasty Origins
920.label: Event
920.description: The Dlamini clan traces origins to the Nguni migration; oral traditions recount founding ancestor Dlamini I; clan establishes authority over neighbouring groups in the Lubombo region.

930.name: Formation of the Swazi Kingdom
930.label: Event
930.description: The Swazi kingdom crystallises under Ngwane III and expands dramatically under Sobhuza I and Mswati II, navigating the turbulent Mfecane era.

930.name: Ngwane III and Kingdom Foundation
930.label: Event
930.description: Ngwane III (considered the first king of Swaziland) leads the Dlamini across the Lubombo Mountains into present-day Eswatini; establishes the kingdom's territorial core.

930.name: Sobhuza I and the Mfecane
930.label: Event
930.description: Sobhuza I (Somhlolo) navigates Zulu expansion during the Mfecane; moves capital northward; builds alliances through diplomacy and intermarriage rather than war.

940.name: Colonial Concessions and British Protectorate
940.label: Event
940.description: Concession-era exploitation, dual British-Boer administration, and British protectorate status; land alienation devastates Swazi livelihoods.

940.name: Concessions Era and Land Alienation
940.label: Event
940.description: King Mbandzeni grants sweeping land and mineral concessions to European settlers, eventually signing away two-thirds of the kingdom; dual Boer-British administration after 1894.

940.name: British Protectorate of Swaziland
940.label: Event
940.description: Britain assumes direct control after Anglo-Boer War; Sobhuza II crowned 1921; fights land concession partition in Privy Council; resistance to incorporation into South Africa.

950.name: Independence and Sobhuza II's Rule
950.label: Event
950.description: Swaziland gains independence in 1968; Sobhuza II suspends the constitution in 1973 and establishes the tinkhundla system; rules until his death in 1982.

950.name: Swaziland Independence 1968
950.label: Event
950.description: Constitutional negotiations; Imbokodvo National Movement wins pre-independence elections; Swaziland becomes independent on 6 September 1968 with Sobhuza II as king.

950.name: 1973 Constitution Suspended
950.label: Event
950.description: Sobhuza II suspends the Westminster-style constitution after opposition NNLC wins parliamentary seats; bans political parties; rules by decree; introduces tinkhundla (regional councils) system.

960.name: Mswati III and Absolute Monarchy
960.label: Event
960.description: Mswati III becomes Africa's last absolute monarch; lavish spending contrasts with extreme poverty; 2005 constitution retains ban on political parties.

960.name: Mswati III's Coronation and Early Rule
960.label: Event
960.description: Crowned at 18 as world's youngest monarch; maintains tinkhundla non-party system; annual Reed Dance (Umhlanga) ceremony showcases royal tradition and draws controversy.

960.name: Reed Dance (Umhlanga) and Cultural Traditions
960.label: Event
960.description: Annual ceremony where young women present reeds to the queen mother; celebration of chastity and Swazi culture; Mswati III selects wives from participants; international debate over women's rights.

960.name: Pro-Democracy Movement and Protests
960.label: Event
960.description: Growing pro-democracy movement challenges absolute monarchy; 2021 protests met with lethal force; name change from Swaziland to Eswatini in 2018.

960.name: Swaziland Renamed Eswatini 2018
960.label: Event
960.description: King Mswati III announces renaming from Swaziland to the Kingdom of Eswatini on 50th anniversary of independence, restoring the original siSwati name.

960.name: 2021 Pro-Democracy Uprising
960.label: Event
960.description: Nationwide protests demanding democratic reforms; security forces kill dozens; internet shutdowns; petitions to parliament; Southern African leaders attempt mediation.
